messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Heads-up problem in GGIR 3.1-3 and 3.1-4
parts:
Dear all,

Hereby I would like to inform you about a problem with the recent GGIR 3.1-3 (only on GitHub August 14) and 3.1-4 (on both CRAN and GitHub).

In release 3.1-3 I added parameter 'nonwear_range_threshold' to allow user-control over the range threshold of the non-wear detection algorithm, and while doing this I also changed its default value to 50 mg because that seemed a great idea at the time.

However, we have now learnt that it was a bad idea as it prevents non-wear detection in some recordings. Therefore, in the upcoming 3.1-5 release I will reverse this to what it has been for the past 10 years (150 mg). 

In the meantime if you were using GGIR 3.1-3  or 3.1-4 you can set nonwear_range_threshold to 150 to reverse the mistake.

Apologies for any inconvenience this may cause.

In an attempt to reduce the risk for similar mistakes in the future I have now assembled a GGIR user panel who I will inform about upcoming updates 2 weeks prior to each new release. If any update is not well motivated to them it will give us the opportunity to reconsider an update.

What could also help is if more people with an interest in R programming made an effort to dive into the GGIR code and tried to help improve it or its documentation. Only then an open-source project like GGIR can thrive.

Best regards,

Vincent

parts:
Hi Vincent

Thank you for this update. I just want to confirm with you the default value for past versions of the package. According to the first publication that described the non-wear detection and the training materials, my understanding is that the range value has always been defined as 50 mg instead of 150 mg by default. The same value (50 mg) has also been reported in all other publications. So I am a bit confused with the changes that you mentioned here with the most recent version of the package?


Thank you.

Best regards,
John.

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Heads-up problem in GGIR 3.1-3 and 3.1-4
parts:
Hi John,

We have always used 50 mg for the non-commercial GENEA accelerometer and 150 mg for all other sensor brands including GENEActiv. Note that GENEActiv is not equal to GENEA, it is an different manufacturer (Unilever Discover R&D department versus ActivInsights Ltd) and comes with different noise level, dynamic range, resolution, and data format. All my PhD publications 2010-2013 were based on GENEA data.

I indeed see we reported 50 mg in 2014 publications for GENEActiv here and here, but that seems to be incorrect. Even in the very first 0.6-17 GGIR release on CRAN in 2013 there was already the distinction between a threshold of 0.05 g for GENEA and a threshold 0.15 g for GENEActiv. You can see by downloading the code https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/GGIR/ and looking at function g.getmeta.R where is has around line 500 the distinction between monitor 1 (GENEA) and monitor 2 (GENEActiv).

I am not sure how we ended up reporting 50 in those 2014 publications. At least it is good to see that we did report the change in standard deviation requirement which went from 3mg in GENEA to 13 mg in GENEActiv.

Best regards,
Vincent
